title: Transfer learning
outcome: By the end, I can explain transfer learning using a traced example and a stated limitation.
scenario: Transfer a fixed feature extractor while identifying what is actually refitted.
given: Frozen extractorh=left+2right. New-task training inputs [1, 0]label0,[2, 1]label0,[1, 3]label1. Class1 whenh>=threshold; candidates3 or5.
All inputs and outcomes in this worked example are invented classroom data; no real model run is claimed.

steps.label: Fit new head
steps.detail: Threshold3 makes1 mistake; threshold 5 makes0, so choose 5.

steps.label: Check held-out input
steps.detail: Query [2, 2]has h = 6, so the head predicts class 1; its reference is not supplied.

explanation: Transfer learning can keep a representation fixed while fitting a smaller output head for a new task. Here the extractor always applies the same weights, while new labels choose the head’s threshold. Applying the chosen head to a query is inference. State which part was frozen and which was fitted; this arithmetic does not establish the extractor is useful for every task.

counterfactual.prediction: Its h becomes4 and the fitted head predicts class 0.
counterfactual.reason: Extractor stays fixed; the changed input crosses the chosen head’s boundary.

student_task: Which part was trained for the new task? Point to the relevant step in the picture, then write the changed result and the rule or evidence that supports it.
teacher_answer: Only the threshold head was selected from the new training labels. The declared extractor weights [1, 2] were frozen. Changed-case check: Its h becomes4 and the fitted head predicts class 0. Extractor stays fixed; the changed input crosses the chosen head’s boundary.
project_evidence: For your Image-pattern Network Investigation, save the input, procedure, observed result and limitation of this check. Label this worked example as practice; use a different, previously unreviewed case when checking independent understanding.
limits: A frozen extractor can miss task-specific distinctions; transfer is a strategy requiring validation, not a guarantee of useful features.
